severity: blocking for the claim statement as worded (not for RESULTS.md)
requirement: reporting contract: what a range is a range of
finding: The statement's ranges 0.70-0.88 / 0.71-0.89 (2^24), 0.79-0.95 / 0.74-0.94 (2^28), 1.05-1.18 / 1.01-1.15 (2^32), the fast/std 4-11% / 0-15% and the BSGS 1.41-1.62x are ranges of cell medians (median over the 4 configurations of each (size, T) cell). The statement never says so and sets them beside per-configuration counts ('faster in 12 of 12 configurations'), so they read as per-configuration ranges. Per configuration the IC/rho ratio is 0.70-0.98 (std) / 0.70-0.97 (fast) at 2^24, 0.77-0.99 / 0.72-0.98 at 2^28 and 1.03-1.19 / 1.00-1.17 at 2^32; IC fast/std 0.82-0.98, rho fast/std 0.81-1.07, IC/BSGS 1.31-1.67. The statement also drops the disclosure the validated predecessor carried: each cell decision is a 4-of-4 sign rule (the bootstrap interval of a median of 4 equals their range). RESULTS.md labels its table 'median of 4 per cell' and gives the per-configuration ranges, so RESULTS itself is correct.
amendment: say 'cell medians (median over the 4 configurations of each size-T cell)' and state the 4-of-4 sign rule; see claim-report.json proposed_wording

finding: (a) The A/A noise figure 'median |log(repeat/median)| over all keys is 0.008' is computed as stated, but with 3 repeats one term per key is the median itself (exactly 0), so a third of the terms are zero; over the two non-median repeats the median is 0.020 (95th percentile 0.12). (b) 'The IC/rho effects at 2^24 (12-30%) and 2^32 (5-20%) are larger than the drift': at 2^32 the fast build's T = 1024 cell is 1.011 (1%), not larger than the ~3% drift; and '5-20%' combines the std cell medians (5-18%) with a per-configuration maximum (19.5%).
amendment: report 0.020 (non-median repeats) beside 0.008; 'at 2^32 5-18% (std) and 1-15% (fast) by cell median; the fast build's 2^32 T = 1024 cell (1%) is within the drift'
